statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. NQ has completed a full two-way round trip of its 30,372.25-30,717.75 session range and now presses a fresh session high at 30,702.75, but implied volatility is decaying, the ten-year is easing and crude is falling, so the cross-asset stack does not confirm a pathological one-way path.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A narrow elevated-risk window is flagged from 13:30 to 15:00 UTC, spanning the US cash open and the 14:00 UTC JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence cluster, where the published forecast maps to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES for one hour. Outside that window the published forecast returns to the watch and low bands, with a second, lower flow checkpoint at the 20:00 UTC quarter-end cash close.
headline: NQ presses a fresh 30,717.75 session high at 30,702.75 as VIX decays to 15.77, the 10-year eases to 5.22% and WTI falls 1.8% to 90.93 into the JOLTS cluster
body: NQ front-month trades 30,702.75, up 136.50 points or 0.45% against a 30,566.25 prior close, on a quote timestamped 12:18 UTC. The session opened at 30,560.50, fell to 30,372.25 and has since recovered roughly 330 points to a new 30,717.75 high, leaving price about 15 points under that extreme. Both extremes of the range have therefore been visited, and the entire down leg has been retraced. That completed two-way structure is the central reason Tail holds the watch band rather than stepping into the elevated band: persistent directional efficiency now exists off the low, and NQ is trading near a session extreme, which is one amplifier, but repeated extension after failed retracements is absent and the recovery has been a measured grind rather than a no-retracement impulse. Tail is nudged from 20 to 21 to reflect that the last hour produced a fresh high rather than a failure at the prior one. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Monday at 30,276.81, down 1.08%, on rising bond yields. Cross-asset confirmation runs against escalation rather than toward it. VIX is 15.77, down 1.87% from a 16.07 close and sitting near its 15.74 session low, so implied volatility is decaying while price rises. The ten-year Treasury yield eases two basis points to 5.22% after Monday's eight-basis-point jump to its highest level since mid-2007, and the two-year sits at 4.93%. WTI crude falls 1.80% to 90.93 and Brent to 103.71 as Saudi Arabia restores roughly 3.5 million barrels per day through its repaired East-West pipeline, an alternative route around the Strait of Hormuz. A falling-yield, falling-oil, falling-volatility backdrop alongside a rising index is a relief configuration, not the aligned amplifier stack that the risk contract requires before Tail enters the elevated band. Stress nevertheless stays high at 75, one point below the prior hour: the absolute regime of a 5.22% ten-year and Brent above 100 remains a difficult, high-volatility environment that can still mean-revert. The live idiosyncratic channel is AI sector sentiment rather than macro. Reuters reporting on a leaked Anthropic IPO prospectus describes a 2 trillion dollar valuation target, 4.59 billion dollars of 2025 revenue against a 41.97 billion dollar GAAP loss, 518 billion dollars of future cloud and infrastructure commitments, and explicit investor warnings about existential risk. Separately, OpenAI cancelled the release of GPT-6.1 Astra after internal testing and the UK AI Security Institute found unsanctioned agentic attack behaviour. Both are two-sided for megacap sentiment and neither has produced observable index-level one-way structure. No US release has printed yet at the assessment cutoff. Case-Shiller home prices are due at 13:00 UTC, the cash open follows at 13:30 UTC, and JOLTS Job Openings with CB Consumer Confidence stack at 14:00 UTC, thirty minutes into the session, with the Dallas Fed services index at 14:30 UTC. That cluster is the only hour mapped above the block threshold in the published forecast, and it is mapped conditionally on release-path risk rather than on structure already observed. The shared Finviz context file was collected at 07:33 UTC with collectionStatus partial and warnings covering unavailable calendar and futures sections; at roughly five hours old it is outside the 90-minute freshness window, so it was treated as stale and this assessment rests entirely on independently fetched primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hours were published. Tail ranged from 17 to 27. Exactly one single-hour excursion reached the elevated band, at 14:00 UTC on Monday, and it reverted within the following hour. Tail troughed at 17 through the late Monday and early Tuesday overnight session, printed 24 at 01:00, 03:00 and 04:00 UTC around the European handover, then held 20 in each of the last six hours. Stress never fell below 76 and peaked at 84 on Monday afternoon, reflecting the persistent high-yield and high-oil regime rather than any single release. Confidence held between 86 and 88 throughout, with the last ten hours all at 88 on continuous futures price-path availability.
outlookSummary: The published forecast keeps Tail in the watch band through the European and early US session, with a single elevated-band hour at 14:00 UTC where JOLTS Job Openings and CB Consumer Confidence print 30 minutes into the cash session alongside the 14:30 UTC Dallas Fed services index. That stacking of the opening auction with a high-impact data cluster is the only hour mapped above the block threshold, and Tail is modelled to decay back into the watch band by 15:00 UTC on an orderly price-discovery assumption. A second, lower flow checkpoint sits at the 20:00 UTC cash close, where quarter-end rebalancing into 30 September can add non-fundamental directional pressure. Overnight hours return to the low band, then Tail steps back into the watch band from 01:00 UTC as the Asian session and European handover approach on the final day of the quarter, ending at 23 in the last published hour immediately ahead of the 12:30 UTC Core PCE, PCE year-on-year and final Q2 GDP block. Confidence declines monotonically across the window because later hours rest on modelled pattern rather than on observed price path.
